stem: A client asks what a stool-based occult-blood colorectal cancer screening test does. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: FIT and high-sensitivity guaiac testing detect blood in stool, and an abnormal screening result requires colonoscopy for further evaluation.
options.B: A positive stool test confirms colorectal cancer, so additional visualization of the colon is not needed to establish the diagnosis.
options.C: The stool test directly visualizes the colon and allows polyps to be removed during the same screening procedure when they are found.
options.D: A negative stool result ends the need for future colorectal-cancer screening because repeat testing is not part of stool-based strategies.

rationale: The current USPSTF colorectal-cancer screening recommendation states that high-sensitivity guaiac fecal occult blood testing and fecal immunochemical testing detect blood in stool. It also states that abnormal stool-based screening results require follow-up colonoscopy for further evaluation. Therefore A is correct. A stool test does not directly visualize the colon or remove polyps, does not independently confirm cancer, and a negative result does not permanently end screening because stool-based strategies are repeated at recommended intervals.
educational_objective: Explain that stool-based occult-blood colorectal-cancer screening detects blood in stool and that abnormal results require diagnostic follow-up with colonoscopy.
source_document_title: Colorectal Cancer: Screening — Final Recommendation Statement
source_version_date: Published May 18, 2021; current official USPSTF page live-rechecked 2026-08-26
source_locator: Screening Tests > Stool-Based Tests: high-sensitivity gFOBT and FIT detect blood in stool; when stool-based tests reveal abnormal results, follow-up colonoscopy is needed for further evaluation. Clinician Summary lists repeat screening intervals.
source_claim_supported: FIT and high-sensitivity gFOBT detect blood in stool, and abnormal stool-based screening results require follow-up colonoscopy.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic/screening test teaching and follow-up.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths while preserving the exact USPSTF distinction between stool screening and required colonoscopy follow-up after abnormal results.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — USPSTF explicitly states both the stool-test purpose and colonoscopy follow-up requirement; no alternate option is defensible.
